title: AI software measures pure ground-glass nodules to predict invasive adenocarcinoma on CT
summary: In 388 pure ground-glass nodules from three centers, commercial deep learning software measured diameter, volume, attenuation and mass; AI and radiologist diameters agreed (ICC 0.972 to 0.981). Mass gave the best AUCs: 0.915 (training), 0.913 (testing) and 0.893 in the 91-nodule external cohort. The study is retrospective and the software is a measurement tool.
ai_technology: Commercial deep learning software for nodule detection, segmentation and quantitative measurement on low-dose CT
organization: Sichuan Cancer Hospital & Institute, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

evidence.tested: Testing and external validation cohorts against pathology.
evidence.unknown: Effect on screening management is not tested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Segmented nodules and extracted quantitative measures used to predict invasiveness.
